description:
Runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and other terminal coding agents together on one mission.

Runner is a native desktop application where terminal agents work together. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI and pi can take the same task in one mission, and each agent keeps its own TUI in a real terminal while the lead brings the decisions back to you. Everything in Runner is also a `runner` command: missions, crews, roles, projects, chats, sessions and messages are all addressable from the command line, with `runnerd` as the background service. Agents run natively on Windows without WSL, and PowerShell 7 is optional. Status: alpha, actively shipping. Native builds target macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) on Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Intel Macs, Windows ARM64 and Linux are not supported. The installer, the application and the CLI sidecars are Authenticode-signed with a Certum open-source certificate issued to Open Source Developer Yicheng Wang.
Runner 0.20.2 is a feature release for macOS, Windows and Linux on top of 0.20.1. It brings git worktrees into the app, reads Codex's status from Codex's own terminal reports, and finishes the fix for remote control dropping and the app hanging.
New
- Git worktrees in the app. When you start a local chat, terminal or mission inside a Git repository, a Checkout control in the launcher's Location row lets you stay in the main checkout, pick an existing worktree, or choose New worktree… to create a linked worktree under .worktrees/ from a new branch and a base branch. In the sidebar's Projects view, a session in a linked worktree shows its branch on a second line; in Active, the branch replaces the subfolder. Archiving the last chat, tab or mission in a worktree Runner created offers Remove worktree in its confirmation, checked by default. A remote chat in a worktree shows the host's branch and base in Info. (#1213)
- Codex status comes from Codex itself. Runner now reads Codex's built-in status reports in chats and missions instead of installing status hooks, so Codex sessions show Approval needed, Answer needed, unread completion badges and Response failed. Codex's Status hooks switch is gone from Settings → Agents → Launch. Claude Code and pi chats with Status hooks off now also show waits, failures and unread completion badges from the agent's terminal status. Runner now requires Codex 0.164.0 or newer; an older Codex shows Update needed and is updated when you start it. (#1320)
Bug fixes
- Remote control no longer drops and hangs the app. 0.20.1 fixed one cause; this release fixes the rest. A slow or stuck remote channel no longer stalls the other channels or the connection, the background service no longer holds the database while it waits on a session, and the app's windows no longer wait on the service for routine refreshes. Runner also logs slow service steps and app stalls to help diagnose any that remain. (#1377)
- Remote control survives a trip to Settings. Opening this computer's Settings from a remote window and going back returns you to the same remote tab with terminal control intact. (#1385)
- ⌘W closes the focused mission drawer shell. In a mission's terminal drawer, ⌘W (Ctrl+Shift+W on Windows and Linux) now closes the focused shell tab, like its ×, instead of hiding the whole drawer. (#1398)
- Choosing a project always takes its folder. Picking a project in the launcher now starts in that project's folder even when the current folder is inside it, so a parent folder registered as a project no longer leaves you in one of its repositories. No project returns to your default working directory, or your home folder when that setting is blank. (#1392)
- Reordering remote projects in the sidebar. Dragging a project in a remote computer's sidebar now shows drop positions above and below each project, not only at the bottom. (#1395)
- Linux: softer window shadow. Floating windows on light desktops no longer show a hard gray edge where the shadow ends. (#1387)
